frase_inicial: Timothy and Melanie: let's take one small step together today, starting with something simple.

tarjetas.frente: Card with high interest needs attention
tarjetas.reverso: That credit card is costing you both money each month. Paying some cash toward it will cut what you lose and free income for other goals.
tarjetas.detalle: Pay $6,800 on the 18% Chase card from cash to reduce high revolving exposure; leaves $11,200 on card per plan.

tarjetas.frente: Life cover for the family is thin
tarjetas.reverso: If either of you died, Liam and Josh would lose a large part of the household income. Adding life cover protects the kids and your ability to keep plans on track.
tarjetas.detalle: Add $235,000 of life cover to bring total to $485,000; after card paydown life cover should reach $491,800 to clear the gate.

tarjetas.frente: You have a strong cash cushion
tarjetas.reverso: Your cash already covers many months of essentials. That gives you a safe source to use for a few protection fixes without risking daily life.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash today: $150,800; recommended emergency reserve: 8–9 months; cash above reserve and short-term goals: $60,222.50.

tarjetas.frente: No umbrella policy for big liability claims
tarjetas.reverso: A large claim could touch the savings you are holding for the kids. Buying extra liability cover shields your cash and home from that risk.
tarjetas.detalle: Umbrella gap per plan: $1,000,000; no umbrella policy in place today.

tarjetas.frente: College saving still needs a plan
tarjetas.reverso: Nothing is set aside yet for Liam and Josh's college. Decide how education shares your spare cash so you both know whether to save now or later.
tarjetas.detalle: College funding gap: $113,508.60; extra yearly saving needed first year: $4,609.22.

tarjetas.reverso: Your retirement plan looks solid and captures the employer matches. For now, you can focus spare cash on protection and the card without changing retirement saving.
tarjetas.detalle: Combined retirement savings rate: 22.8% of income; plan projects savings last through retirement.

tarjetas.frente: Invested mix is more aggressive than Melanie prefers
tarjetas.reverso: Timothy and Melanie have different comfort with swings. Agreeing together on how much ups-and-downs you accept will help both sleep better and keep the plan steady.
tarjetas.detalle: Household long-term portfolio about 77% stocks; Timothy growth, Melanie moderate.

tarjetas.reverso: A new car and a home are planned in coming years. Keep those dates in mind when choosing whether to use cash now or hold some for those payments.
tarjetas.detalle: Vehicle planned 2028; home planned 2030 per goals.

tarjetas.frente: There is spare cash above needs you can use
tarjetas.reverso: You’re not short on a basic cushion. That spare money can pay down expensive card debt or start life cover without touching daily spending.
tarjetas.detalle: Cash above emergency reserve and vacation goal: $60,222.50 available today.
